1	# fizeau-harbor-runner: wraps Harbor + Fizeau's Python adapters so the host
2	# stops needing a Python toolchain to drive bench runs.
3	#
4	# Resolved pin: harbor==0.3.0 from PyPI. The bead description mentioned
5	# "harbor-bench" but no such package is published; the Harbor CLI ships as
6	# `harbor` on PyPI, and Fizeau's harbor_agent.py already targets the 0.3.x
7	# BaseInstalledAgent API (see scripts/benchmark/harbor_agent.py:3).
8	FROM python:3.12-slim
9	
10	RUN pip install --no-cache-dir harbor==0.3.0
11	
12	COPY scripts/benchmark/harbor_adapters/ /app/harbor_adapters/
13	COPY scripts/benchmark/harbor_agent.py /app/harbor_agent.py
14	
15	ENV PYTHONPATH=/app
16	WORKDIR /app
17	
18	ENTRYPOINT ["harbor"]

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# Acceptance tests for fizeau-harbor-runner Docker image build and content-sha label

# Resolve absolute paths
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && cd .. && pwd)"
BUILD_SCRIPT="${SCRIPT_DIR}/build-harbor-runner.sh"
IMAGE_TAG="fizeau-harbor-runner:latest"

# Test 1: build-harbor-runner.sh produces the image and harbor --help exits 0
@test "Test_harbor_runner_image_builds" {
  # Build the image
  bash "${BUILD_SCRIPT}"

  # Verify image exists via docker inspect
  docker inspect "${IMAGE_TAG}" >/dev/null

  # Verify docker run --rm fizeau-harbor-runner:latest --help exits 0
  docker run --rm "${IMAGE_TAG}" --help >/dev/null
  [ $? -eq 0 ]
}

# Test 2: the image's image-content-sha label equals computed sha256
@test "Test_image_label_matches_content_sha" {
  # Build the image and capture the content-sha output
  local build_output
  build_output=$(bash "${BUILD_SCRIPT}" 2>&1)

  # Extract the image-content-sha from build output
  local reported_sha
  reported_sha=$(echo "$build_output" | grep -oP 'image-content-sha=\K[a-f0-9]+')
  [ -n "$reported_sha" ]

  # Get the actual label from the built image
  local actual_label
  actual_label=$(docker inspect --format='{{index .Config.Labels "image-content-sha"}}' "${IMAGE_TAG}")
  [ -n "$actual_label" ]
  [ "$actual_label" != "<nil>" ]

  # Verify they match
  [ "$reported_sha" = "$actual_label" ]
}

# Test 3: mutating harbor_adapters changes the content sha
@test "Test_label_changes_when_adapter_changes" {
  # Get the initial content-sha
  local initial_sha
  initial_sha=$(docker inspect --format='{{index .Config.Labels "image-content-sha"}}' "${IMAGE_TAG}")

  # Backup an adapter file
  local adapter_file="${SCRIPT_DIR}/harbor_adapters/claude.py"
  local backup_file="${adapter_file}.bak"
  cp "$adapter_file" "$backup_file"

  # Modify the adapter file (add a comment to change content)
  echo "# Modified for test" >> "$adapter_file"

  # Compute the new content-sha (simulate what build-harbor-runner.sh does)
  local new_sha
  new_sha=$(bash "${BUILD_SCRIPT}" 2>&1 | grep -oP 'image-content-sha=\K[a-f0-9]+')

  # Restore the adapter file
  mv "$backup_file" "$adapter_file"

  # Verify the sha changed
  [ "$initial_sha" != "$new_sha" ]
}

# Test 3: mutating harbor_adapters changes the computed content sha
@test "Test_label_changes_when_adapter_changes" {
  # Helper function to compute content sha (mimic build-harbor-runner.sh logic)
  compute_content_sha() {
    local adapters_dir="$1"
    local harbor_agent="$2"
    local dockerfile="$3"
    {
      LC_ALL=C find "$adapters_dir" -type f \
        | LC_ALL=C sort \
        | while IFS= read -r f; do
            printf '%s  %s\n' "$(sha256sum "$f" | awk '{print $1}')" "${f#$(dirname "$adapters_dir")/}"
          done
      printf '%s  %s\n' "$(sha256sum "$harbor_agent" | awk '{print $1}')" "harbor_agent.py"
      printf '%s  %s\n' "$(sha256sum "$dockerfile" | awk '{print $1}')" "Dockerfile.harbor-runner"
    } | sha256sum | awk '{print $1}'
  }
